submission.bindingBasis: The planning digest sha256:e5d8008d... differs from currentSourceStateDigest sha256:79bcb09f... The planning binding attempt already failed with REVISION_MISMATCH/not_committed. The tree bytes are identical but the digest differs, so the compare-and-close contract would reject the planning digest. Per the contract, after re-observation a caller may close against the new exact current digest. Re-observation is required to establish the new binding basis.
submission.rationale: The workspace.close contract is a compare-and-close against one exact expected source state digest. The planning-time digest (e5d8008d...) no longer matches the current source state digest (79bcb09f...) because of a concurrent empty Git commit (which changed the head revision and thereby the digest, even though tree bytes are identical). The planning binding attempt already returned REVISION_MISMATCH/not_committed. Trying ACT_WITH_PLANNING_BINDING would predictably fail not_committed. The contract explicitly allows closing against the new exact current digest after re-observation. The difference is only an empty commit with identical tree bytes, so the risk of semantic change is low, but the compare-and-close contract requires the exact current digest. REOBSERVE_THEN_DECIDE is the correct step to obtain the fresh binding basis.
